channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: 3.5 Billion Records Exposed in Two Public Databases
item.description: Researchers uncovered two publicly exposed databases holding more than 3.5 billion records, including stolen passwords, session cookies, and children’s school data. The exposure stemmed from misconfigured access controls that left the databases unauthenticated, enabling credential-stealing attacks. Affected parties must revoke compromised credentials, enforce stricter access policies, and monitor for credential reuse.

item.title: Fake WordPress Plugin Bypasses 2FA, Injects Malicious Scripts
item.description: A counterfeit WordPress plugin enables attackers to bypass two-factor authentication and inject malicious JavaScript into visitor browsers. The hidden plugin exploits the WordPress authentication flow, allowing credential theft and cross-site scripting that can compromise user sessions and data. Security teams should remove the rogue plugin, audit the site for other hidden code, and enforce strict plugin vetting and two-factor enforcement.

item.title: AI Agents Steal Credentials, Breach Corporate Networks
item.description: Hackers used autonomous AI agents to harvest credentials and infiltrate corporate networks across government, logistics, hospitality, manufacturing, agriculture, and education sectors. Agents exploited vulnerable web applications for initial footholds, installed web shells, and performed lateral movement, exposing sensitive data. Defenders should patch web app flaws, monitor for web shells, enforce least privilege, and deploy AI-driven threat detection.

item.title: Tracking AI-Enhanced Hacking Incidents
item.description: Daniel Meissler tracks incidents of hacking that leverage AI tools, documenting offensive tactics employed by attackers. The analysis highlights how AI accelerates reconnaissance, vulnerability exploitation, and automated attack orchestration, increasing campaign speed and scale. Security teams should adopt AI-aware monitoring, threat intelligence feeds, and defensive automation to detect and mitigate AI-driven attacks.

item.title: Credential Remediation Stalls Without Impact Assessment
item.description: GitGuardian’s State of Secrets Sprawl 2026 report shows that 64% of valid secrets from 2022 remained active in January 2026, highlighting slow remediation. Delays stem from teams lacking visibility into downstream breakage, causing validity-only triage to miss 46% of critical secrets and raising credential misuse risk. Impact-based prioritization and automated breakage testing can accelerate revocation and reduce credential theft exposure.

item.title: Drupal Core RCE CVE-2026-132165 Exploited in Wild
item.description: Drupal core suffers remote code execution via Fail2Install, identified as CVE-2026-132165, actively exploited in the wild. The flaw, rated CVSS 9.8, allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary PHP code, jeopardizing site integrity and data confidentiality. CISA mandates federal agencies to apply the vendor patch by November 27, 2026, and recommends disabling the vulnerable module until the update is installed.

item.title: Bots exploited leaked AWS key from Docker image in under 8 seconds
item.description: A cloud access key left inside a newly published Docker image can be found and used by bots in less than eight seconds, Billy Tsouvalas and Nick Nikiforakis of Stony Brook University discovered after planting 300 decoy images on public container registries.

item.title: Microsoft 365 Bug Blocking Office Apps Fixed
item.description: Microsoft released a patch for a Microsoft 365 bug that prevented certain customers from accessing Office applications. The flaw caused authentication failures in the Office client, leading to denial of service for affected users. Users should install the latest update from Microsoft 365 and verify application access to restore functionality.

item.title: Pierre Cadieux Traces Security Roots in Help Desk Logs
item.description: Pierre Cadieux reflects on his early help-desk career, where he first learned to correlate Windows and Unix logs. This foundational skill sparked his curiosity and ultimately guided him toward a career in cybersecurity. The article highlights the importance of cross-platform log analysis for early security insight and career development today.

item.title: OpenAI-Linked Swarm Activity Traceable via Public Records
item.description: OpenAI-linked swarm activity observed in 2026 is fully traceable through public records, according to a Cisco Talos blog. The analysis compares the swarm’s tradecraft to early signals from current agentic attack activity, highlighting patterns in data exfiltration, command-and-control, and persistence. Security teams can use the documented tradecraft indicators to refine detection rules and improve attribution of future agentic attacks.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical PHP Update for RHEL 9.8
item.description: Red Hat released a critical PHP security update for RHEL 9.8 EUS, addressing multiple high-severity flaws. The patch carries a CVSS base score indicating critical impact, and each vulnerability is referenced by a CVE identifier in the advisory’s references. Security teams should apply the patch immediately to mitigate exploitation of the PHP flaws.

item.title: Critical 9.9 Dell Enterprise SONiC Flaw Could Let Hackers Execute Malicious Commands on Network Switches
item.description: Dell Technologies has patched a critical flaw in Dell Enterprise SONiC Distribution that could let a remote attacker with limited privileges run commands of their choice on an affected network switch. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-103782, could also expose files and directories the attacker is not authorized to access.

item.title: Drupal RCE Flaw Exploited to Hijack Sites
item.description: A critical Drupal RCE vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild to hijack unpatched sites. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution via crafted requests, giving attackers full site control; it has a CVSS score of 9.8. Drupal released a patch; administrators must update immediately and verify configuration to block exploitation.

item.title: RHSA-2026:103485: Important: cifs-utils security update
item.description: An update for cifs-utils is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.2 Extended Update Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Anthropic Beta Release Detects Malicious AI Activity Securely
item.description: Anthropic launched a public beta of Enterprise Frontier Safeguards to help organizations detect harmful artificial intelligence activity. The system analyzes customer-controlled cloud conversations to flag suspicious behaviors while preserving zero data retention through customer-managed encryption keys. Enterprise security teams can implement the platform to monitor multi-interaction threat patterns without exposing sensitive internal data to external retention.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102933: Low: dhcp security update
item.description: An update for dhcp is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Low. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Hex.pm RCE Flaw Compromises Six Package Registry Servers
item.description: An attacker ran OS commands on six Hex.pm servers by exploiting a CVSS 10.0 RCE flaw. The flaw, present since February 2016, allows unauthenticated remote code execution via crafted API requests, enabling full system compromise. Hex.pm applied a patched build within 15 minutes of the first request; administrators should ensure all servers run the latest release.

item.title: Idunno AntiCsrf Library RCE Exploited via CVE-2026-131914
item.description: Attackers exploit CVE-2026-131914 in the defunct Idunno AntiCsrf library to achieve remote code execution. The flaw permits execution of arbitrary code through a single crafted web request, enabling full server compromise without authentication. Since the library is defunct, developers should remove Idunno dependencies and apply the vendor patch or migrate to a maintained CSRF solution.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102924: Important: gdm security, bug fix, and enhancement update
item.description: An update for gdm is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102930: Important: qt5-qtdeclarative security update
item.description: An update for qt5-qtdeclarative is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.8 Update Services for SAP Solutions and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.8 Telecommunications Update Service. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important.

item.title: Microsoft Reports Authentication Issues Post-November Updates
item.description: Microsoft customers may experience authentication failures after installing November security updates that fixed a high-severity RCE vulnerability. The updates alter authentication components, causing intermittent login errors for some users; the issue is unrelated to the RCE fix. Microsoft recommends applying the latest cumulative update and monitoring login problems while a hotfix is under investigation.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Thunderbird Update for Enterprise Linux 8.8
item.description: Red Hat released a security, bug fix, and enhancement update for Thunderbird on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.8. Red Hat Product Security rated the underlying security flaws with an Important impact severity rating based on CVSS scoring standards. Enterprise security teams utilizing SAP Solutions and Telecommunications Update Service streams should apply the newly issued software update.

item.title: Police Shut Down 57 IPTV Services, Trace €26M Crypto
item.description: Police from 11 countries disrupted 57 IPTV services and identified 321 pirate sites during a five-day Europol operation in Seville. The operation traced over €26 million in crypto payments, revealing the financial backbone of the streaming network and anonymized wallet usage. No arrests announced; transaction analysis remains ongoing, underscoring the need for continued crypto flow monitoring to deter piracy.

item.title: RHSA-2026:103484: Important: raptor2 security update
item.description: An update for raptor2 is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.6 Extended Update Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Palo Alto Releases Patch for Fragnesia Rooting Flaw
item.description: Palo Alto Networks issued a patch for the Fragnesia kernel flaw, CVE-2026-46300, which attackers used to gain root access on PAN-OS firewalls. The flaw enabled unauthenticated code execution via exposed management interfaces, allowing full system compromise in affected devices. Customers should apply the latest PAN-OS update and restrict internet-reachable management interfaces to prevent exploitation.

item.title: Hackers Exploit Fragnesia Kernel Flaw for Firewall Root Access
item.description: Hackers are exploiting the Fragnesia Linux kernel flaw, CVE-2026-46300, to gain root access on Palo Alto Networks firewalls running PAN-OS. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute privileged code via exposed management interfaces, enabling full system compromise. Palo Alto urges immediate patching and restriction of internet-reachable management interfaces to mitigate the vulnerability.

item.title: Anthropic Scanner Discovers Drupal Flaw, Attacks Exploit It
item.description: CISA added a Drupal core vulnerability, discovered by an Anthropic scanner, to its KEV catalog after attackers exploited it in multiple incidents. The flaw permits remote code execution on affected Drupal installations, enabling attackers to compromise site integrity and data. Federal agencies must apply the latest Drupal security patch within three days to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Hackers Use Stolen AI Prompt Data to Search AWS Cloud Storage and Secret Management Services
item.description: Hackers used Amazon Web Services (AWS) access keys stolen from AI prompts to list cloud storage buckets and search services that hold passwords, API tokens, and application settings. Security firm Dragos traced the activity to credentials it had planted in test prompts.

item.title: CIA Open-Source Analysis System Breached by Unknown Attackers
item.description: Unknown attackers breached the CIA’s open-source intelligence analysis system, exposing internal analytical tools. The intrusion leveraged undisclosed vulnerabilities, allowing unauthorized access to classified analytical data, though the exact exploit vector remains unreported. The CIA has not yet issued a public patch or detailed mitigation guidance, leaving security teams uncertain about immediate countermeasures.

item.title: Top 10 Managed Vulnerability Scanning Services Ranked 2026
item.description: The article ranks the top ten managed vulnerability scanning services for 2026, highlighting credentialed scanning reliability and production-friendly result triage. It discusses how these services filter false positives, streamline triage, and reduce operational overhead for security teams. Readers can compare scoring criteria, pricing models, and integration capabilities to select a solution that aligns with their risk appetite.

item.title: Idunno AntiCsrf Library Exploited for ASP.NET RCE
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-131914, a deserialization flaw in the abandoned Idunno AntiCsrf library, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, exposing legacy ASP.NET applications to remote code execution. The vulnerability permits attackers to deserialize untrusted data, enabling arbitrary code execution without authentication on exposed web services.

item.title: Top 10 PTaaS Platforms Ranked for 2026
item.description: The article ranks the top PTaaS platforms for 2026, emphasizing on-demand human testing and rapid fix retesting. It assesses platforms on tester quality, tool integration, and how quickly findings feed back into development pipelines. Organizations can use the rankings to choose a provider that matches their deployment cadence and security testing maturity.

item.title: Remus Stealer Deploys Malicious Chrome Extension to Steal Gmail Data
item.description: Remus Stealer malware targets compromised Windows systems running Google Chrome by silently deploying a fake Google Sheets extension. The rogue background extension reads incoming Gmail messages from signed-in accounts and exfiltrates email contents to an attacker-controlled server. Security teams must audit Chrome extensions, remove unauthorized add-ons, and monitor Windows endpoints for unauthorized background processes.

item.title: Com-Affiliated Hackers Hijack Cloud Accounts via Vishing for Data Theft and Extortion
item.description: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 has disclosed that it's tracking and has responded to "numerous waves of vishing attacks" orchestrated by Com-affiliated threat actors since August 2026 that have led to data theft and extortion attempts.

item.title: WordPress Blocks Six Backdoored WP Connect Plugins Before Malicious Releases Go Live
item.description: WordPress has removed six WordPress plugins developed by WP Connect after they were backdoored on November 22, 2026, to enable arbitrary code execution on sites that have them installed, following a suspected compromise of the developer's account. The WordPress plugins team has independently detected and blocked the threat before it could be officially released.

item.title: Open-Source GPU Task Manager Released
item.description: gputaskman is a terminal tool that displays GPU memory usage and AI model attribution on Windows, Linux, WSL, and Apple Silicon Macs. Native task managers report only raw memory; gputaskman shows which processes own GPU resources. The project is on GitHub and can be installed via package managers or built from source; no vendor patch needed.

item.title: Security+ Foundations, SSCP Demonstrates Practical Readiness
item.description: The article argues that Security+ certifications provide essential theoretical knowledge, while SSCP demonstrates the ability to apply that knowledge in real-world scenarios. It stresses that operational readiness demands continuous practice, rapid response, and maintaining a 'ready state' amid escalating threats. Readers are encouraged to pursue both foundational and applied certifications to bridge theory and execution.

item.title: Holiday Scam Victims Cut Essentials Amid Rising Losses
item.description: McAfee research shows that 42% of Americans have fallen for holiday shopping scams, a near doubling from 22% the previous year. The study indicates a decline in consumer confidence, with only 75% able to recognize online scams compared to 90% in 2025. The findings highlight the need for heightened consumer education and improved fraud-detection tools to mitigate rising losses.

item.title: Microsoft Declares Code Red Over 24-Hour M365 Outage
item.description: Microsoft announced an internal Code Red after a nearly 24-hour outage of Microsoft 365 services, affecting Outlook, Teams, Copilot, and Exchange Online on November 12-13, 2026. The incident prompted Microsoft to prioritize rapid recovery and prevent future service disruptions, with CEO Satya Nadella apologizing. Security teams should monitor service health dashboards and review incident response plans for Microsoft 365 deployments.

item.title: CIA, ODNI Breach Exposes Unclassified Intelligence Data
item.description: The CIA and ODNI experienced a cyber intrusion that exposed unclassified intelligence information on a shared analysis network. The attack leveraged vulnerabilities in the shared network’s security controls, allowing attackers to access publicly available material analysis tools without authentication. Investigations are ongoing; agencies are tightening network segmentation, enforcing stricter access controls, and reviewing audit logs to contain the breach.

item.title: ISC Stormcast Podcast Released
item.description: The SANS Internet Storm Center released its weekly Stormcast podcast for Wednesday, November 25, 2026. The episode discusses current threat trends, emerging attack techniques, and analyst insights, offering actionable intelligence for security teams. Listeners can access the full recording and supporting materials through the ISC website link provided in the release.

item.title: Red Hat Satellite Client Critical Update
item.description: Red Hat released a critical security update for Satellite 6 Client to address multiple vulnerabilities affecting the client component. The update is rated Critical by Red Hat Product Security, though specific CVSS scores are not disclosed in the advisory. Users should apply the patch immediately or upgrade to the latest Satellite 6 Client release to mitigate the risks.

item.title: Pan-Alto Fixes OSS CVEs in PAN-OS
item.description: Palo Alto Networks issued PAN-SA-2026-0015, noting that several open-source software CVEs have been fixed in PAN-OS. The bulletin lists the resolved vulnerabilities but provides no CVE identifiers or exploit details, and it is classified as informational. Users should upgrade to the latest PAN-OS version to apply the patches, with no additional workarounds required.

item.title: NGINX HTTP/2 Use-After-Free CVE-2026-123633
item.description: NGINX’s HTTP/2 implementation contains a use-after-free flaw (CVE-2026-123633) that can be triggered by malformed HTTP/2 frames. The vulnerability may allow attackers to crash the server or execute arbitrary code, depending on the context, and is not yet confirmed as actively exploited. NGINX has released a patch for affected versions; administrators should update or apply the provided mitigations to prevent exploitation.

item.title: CIA Unclassified System Breached
item.description: A cyberattack breached an unclassified CIA system, though the specific data compromised and the attacker remain unidentified. The breach indicates potential exploitation of internal network defenses, but no evidence of credential theft or data exfiltration has been disclosed. Security teams should review CIA network hardening measures and monitor for anomalous activity following the incident.

item.title: Red Hat Releases OpenSSL Security Update
item.description: Red Hat has issued a security update for OpenSSL on Red Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update carries a moderate impact rating, with CVSS base scores available via the referenced CVE links, but no active exploitation has been reported. Administrators should apply the patch promptly to maintain OpenSSL security posture and prevent potential exploitation.

item.title: Red Hat Releases librabbitmq Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the librabbitmq library on RHEL 9, fixing vulnerabilities that could enable remote code execution. The flaws involve improper input validation in AMQP handling, with CVSS scores of 7.5-8.3, and are documented but not yet exploited. Apply the latest librabbitmq package immediately to ensure the patched version is in use.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical cjose Update
item.description: Red Hat issued a critical security update for the cjose library on RHEL 9, addressing flaws that could allow remote code execution. The vulnerabilities arise from improper handling of JOSE tokens, with CVSS scores up to 9.1, and are publicly documented but not yet exploited. Red Hat recommends installing the latest cjose package immediately to secure affected systems.

item.title: Satellite Ground Infrastructure Faces Cyber Threats
item.description: Satellite operators face growing cybersecurity risks from weaknesses in ground-based infrastructure that supports space services. These vulnerabilities, including outdated firmware and unsecured communication links, could enable attackers to disrupt satellite operations or intercept data. Operators should update firmware, enforce strict access controls, and conduct regular penetration testing to mitigate emerging threats.

item.title: APT Webworm Customizes SoftEther VPN to Evade Detection
item.description: Webworm, a China-aligned espionage group, rebuilt SoftEther VPN from source, removing default artifacts that would normally alert defenders. By stripping telemetry and logging hooks, the modified VPN hides its presence, enabling stealthy lateral movement inside corporate networks without triggering security monitoring. Security teams should monitor anomalous SoftEther traffic, enforce strict VPN policies, and apply hardening updates that re-enable logging.
